# Worked example: the 1.18.8 release

Dated evidence from one observed release, independently re-verified from live PRs, pipeline status, and PyPI. These are **worked-example values, not universal constants** — a future release will have a different version, SHA, build ID and PR numbers; re-derive each one rather than reusing these.

1. **Baseline.** Before release, PyPI's latest was `1.18.7`; main had an unreleased `1.18.8` changelog section with one bugfix note already present, plus a separately merged fix (#49242) whose note a later commit folded into the same section. Compare `_version.py`, the changelog heading, and merged PRs since the published tag rather than trusting any single source.
2. **Classification/date.** Both pending notes were bug fixes with no public API surface change, so `1.18.8` (patch) was correct; the date became `2026-10-08` only once finalized — the heading was `(Unreleased)` beforehand and must stay that way until the release PR is prepared.
3. **Preparation PR.** The release-preparation PR (#49449, "[azure-ai-evaluation] Release 1.18.8") touched only `CHANGELOG.md`: it dated the heading and folded in the second bugfix note. A minimal, changelog-only diff is expected for a notes/version-only preparation; unrelated file churn should prompt a stop-and-review.
4. **Merge.** The PR merged to main at `dc45c10143afa4b6e4fcd714f0f9866d056ca728`. This is the source commit the release pipeline must build from — verify a candidate run's source SHA against this value, not the run's date or display name.
5. **Pipeline route.** The release used a **manual** run of [python-evaluation](https://dev.azure.com/azure-sdk/internal/_build?definitionId=7162) (build `6938522`, `result: succeeded`), not the post-merge `auto-release`-label route. No `auto-release` label was required for this run; verify which route an owner actually used before describing a release as label-driven.
6. **API review.** `azsdk_package_get_approval_status` for `azure-ai-evaluation 1.18.8` returned API Review Hub `unknownPackage` (primary source does not recognize this package in Python) and APIView (legacy) `isApproved: true`, with a final `Approved: True` sourced from APIView. There was no public API diff for this patch release, so no new review request was needed — the existing approved revision covered it. A different package/version combination, or one with an actual API diff, must still go through the request flow.
7. **Publication.** `GET https://pypi.org/pypi/azure-ai-evaluation/1.18.8/json` returned `bdist_wheel` and `sdist` artifacts, both `yanked: false`. This, plus the verified source SHA, is what makes "released" a defensible claim — a succeeded build alone would not.
8. **Next-version PR.** The template's version-increment PR was #49459, branch `increment-package-version-evaluation-6938522` (build ID embedded, matching step 5's run), merged, bumping `_version.py` to `1.18.9` and adding an empty `## 1.18.9 (Unreleased)` section. An older, still-**open** PR (#49203, branch `...-6883596`, a different build ID) was stale and must not be merged — always match the branch's embedded build ID to the actual release run before trusting an increment PR.
9. **Tracking.** `Prepare-Release.ps1`'s DevOps write happens immediately after the version prompt, before any local edits in step 3 above; this skill does not independently re-verify tracking-system state beyond what the script and PR evidence show.
10. **Cleanup/report.** State observed at each step (local edit, push, PR, merge, build, release stage, publication, next-version PR) rather than inferring later steps from earlier ones; none of the above authorizes repeating these actions for a different release without re-deriving every value above.
